metadata.title: A decade of educational research with the German National Educational Panel Study: A systematic review

survey_design.weight_fields_interpretation: This study is a systematic review of peer-reviewed journal articles that used NEPS data; it does not conduct a secondary analysis on student microdata. Therefore, there is no analytic sample drawn from NEPS microdata and no application of NEPS sampling or replicate weights (e.g., student weights or BRR/jackknife) in the review’s own computations. The review’s quantitative components rely on bibliometric counts and topic-modeling outputs derived from article metadata (titles, abstracts, keywords), not on weighted estimation of achievement or competence scores. For readers intending to conduct NEPS-based empirical analyses, appropriate NEPS sampling weights and complex survey design handling should be applied within each primary study, but such weighting is outside the scope of this review.

data.handling_not_reported_explanation: Plausible Values (PV) are generated for cognitive achievement scales in large-scale assessments, but this paper does not analyze student-level cognitive outcomes from NEPS microdata. Instead, it synthesizes and classifies existing NEPS-related publications using bibliometric procedures and topic modeling on article text. Because there is no PV-based dependent variable in the review, PV handling is not applicable.

sample_details.sample_filtering_criteria: The review’s unit of analysis is peer-reviewed journal articles, not NEPS respondents. Inclusion criteria required: (a) an empirical analysis using NEPS scientific use files (excluding conceptual descriptions and unpublished pilot data), (b) peer-reviewed journal publication (excluding gray literature and non-peer-reviewed items), (c) publication no later than 2024 (excluding advance online without final record), and (d) full text retrievable. The screening process started from 1492 records, removed 664 duplicates, excluded 32 for being published after 2024, excluded 66 for not meeting peer-review, excluded 6 for unavailable full text, and excluded 99 for not reporting empirical NEPS data, yielding 625 included articles.

main_findings.dataset_used: ILSA literature synthesis (systematic review; no single student-level analytic micro-dataset)
main_findings.standardized_conclusion: Using ILSA literature synthesis (systematic review; no single student-level analytic micro-dataset) the study leveraged the reported predictors to predict Literature synthesis outcome (not student-level prediction), finding that This paper is a systematic review of peer-reviewed journal articles that used the German National Educational Panel Study (NEPS) scientific use files. Across 2013–2024, the authors identified 625 eligible NEPS-based publications using a multi-source bibliometric search (NEPS bibliography, OpenAlex, and Scopus) and a transparent screening pipeline (duplicates removed, peer-review and full-text requirements enforced, and empirical NEPS use verified). The review does not estimate effects on student outcomes; instead, it characterizes research volume, prestige/impact (JIF and field-weighted citation index), and thematic structure using topic modeling. Topic modeling was implemented with BERTopic using transformer-based embeddings (SPECTER 2), dimensionality reduction (UMAP), clustering (HDBSCAN), and TF-IDF for topic terms, with topic diversity and semantic coherence reported. Limitations include that the topic-modeling approach is inherently exploratory and may miss underrepresented niche topics, and the review does not evaluate the methodological quality of included primary studies. This indicates that these patterns have implications for educational policy and instructional practice, though cross-sectional ILSA designs cannot establish causality.

data.null_fields_interpretation: This record is a systematic review rather than an empirical ML study on NEPS microdata. Consequently, there is no student-level dataset/cycle/grade/domain, no PV-based achievement outcome, no predictive target variable, and no model performance metrics (e.g., accuracy/RMSE) to extract. The only quantitative modeling reported is topic modeling over article text for bibliometric synthesis, so the schema’s ML predictive fields (main_findings, ml_techniques) are intentionally left empty.
